purpose: Adds wp_cache_flush_runtime() support for admin-only settings changes, avoiding unnecessary persistent cache flushes on shared hosting.
riskRationale: core_tweaks misclassification as admin-only causes stale static HTML cache after disabling emojis/embeds/dashicons – pages already cached would still serve old markup.

text: Well-structured, minimal change following existing codebase patterns. The new flush_runtime() method is correct and properly gated. However, core_tweaks is misclassified as an admin-only tab when its settings (disable emojis, disable embeds, disable dashicons, heartbeat control) directly modify frontend HTML output cached in static files.

reasoning: core_tweaks misclassification causes stale cached pages — moving it to cache_relevant_tabs fixes the issue without changing the architecture.

message: The flush_runtime() method is clean, minimal, and properly gated with function_exists() for WP < 6.0 compatibility – mirrors the existing flush_group() pattern perfectly.
Clean separation of cache-relevant and admin-only tabs with early break optimization – sensible performance consideration.
Correct precedence logic: when both cache-relevant and admin-only tabs change, the full persistent cache clear takes precedence over runtime-only flush.

core_tweaks is incorrectly classified as an admin-only tab. Changes to these settings directly modify frontend HTML output (Core_Tweaks removes emoji detection scripts/styles via wp_head/wp_print_styles, removes embed discovery links/JS, deregisters dashicons on frontend, deregisters heartbeat script). Previously cached static HTML files would still serve the old markup with these scripts/styles, causing stale output until the cache naturally expires or is manually cleared.
suggestion: Move core_tweaks from $admin_only_tabs to $cache_relevant_tabs so changes trigger a full cache clear.
